basics.name: CNC furniture joinery for makers: 'Make: Design for CNC' (book), AtFAB open-source furniture, Opendesk's open furniture library and joinery guides, and dogbone fillet add-ins (Fusion 360 Dogbone)
basics.url: Book: https://filson-rohrbacher.com/work/design-for-cnc (authors' page; designforcnc.com redirects here), https://openlibrary.org/works/OL21571102W, https://books.google.com/books/about/Design_for_CNC.html?id=fRc4DwAAQBAJ. AtFAB: https://filson-rohrbacher.com/work/atfab (atfab.co redirects here). Opendesk: https://opendesk.cc/designs, https://opendesk.cc/blog/digitally-remastered-joinery, https://opendesk.cc/blog/cnc-machines-and-common-cut-types, https://opendesk.cc/blog/design-for-open-making-and-cnc-milling-machines, https://opendesk.cc/about/non-commercial-use, https://opendesk.github.io/design-playground/. Dogbone tools: https://github.com/DVE2000/Dogbone (current Fusion 360 add-in; read via raw.githubusercontent.com), https://github.com/pludikar/dogbone2, http://fablab.ruc.dk/more-elegant-cnc-dogbones/
basics.resource_type: book (Design for CNC) + open furniture model libraries (AtFAB, Opendesk) with illustrated joinery guides + CAD add-in (Fusion 360 Dogbone)
basics.cost: Book: paid (print and ebook; price not verified) [uncertain]. AtFAB files: free download after an email sign-up. Opendesk: some designs downloadable free for non-commercial making, others by request; finished furniture is sold through its maker network. Dogbone add-in: free (MIT licence; Fusion 360 itself needs a free personal or paid licence)
basics.license: Book: all rights reserved (Make Community / O'Reilly), cite only. AtFAB files: described as open source and 'creative-commons' in press coverage, exact licence not verified on an opened page [uncertain]. Opendesk: licence chosen per designer and bundled with each download; many are Creative Commons Non-Commercial, and an Internet Archive collection of Opendesk files lists Lean Desk, Divide, Hot Desk, Unit Table, Fin range, Slim Chair etc. as CC BY and Pedestal and Wiki Booth as CC0. Opendesk blog text and illustrations: no licence shown, treat as all rights reserved. Dogbone add-ins: MIT licence (README)
basics.year: AtFAB started 2008 (authors' page; other sources say 2010); Opendesk founded around 2013 [uncertain], joinery blog series dated 25 September 2017; Design for CNC published 2 October 2017 (Make Community, 344 pages, ISBN 9781457187421); FabLab RUC minimal dogbones post 19 March 2017; Dogbone add-in developed from Casey Rogers' original to version 2.4 (DVE2000 repo); Opendesk site rebuilt around 2025 (image uploads dated 2025)
basics.access_barrier: Book: paywall (purchase or O'Reilly subscription; O'Reilly pages refused access from this environment). AtFAB: free email sign-up for file packages. Opendesk: none to read guides; downloads limited and some by request. Dogbone: desktop install of Autodesk Fusion 360
basics.image_license: Opendesk joint illustrations (clean isometric line drawings of each joint exploded and assembled) and book figures: all rights reserved, link only. Dogbone README images: in an MIT-licensed repo [uncertain whether images are covered]
basics.authority_level: educator and professional designers: Filson & Rohrbacher are architects/designers and the book is a Make: publication; Opendesk is a commercial platform whose lead designer (Josh Worley) wrote the joinery guides; dogbone tools are community open source; FabLab RUC is a university fab lab

coverage.covers: Joints for furniture cut from plywood sheets on a 3-axis CNC router, and the corner treatments that make them fit. Design for CNC: a chapter 'Precision-Fit Plywood Joinery' covering tool diameter, fillets and toolpaths, plus 'eight basic CNC joint conditions' for flat parts (reported as overlap, edge to edge, edge-to-edge-to-edge, end to face, end to face to edge, through, three-way, four-way) and assemblies (S/Z joint, tab, hanger, corner and foot assemblies), taught through stools, chairs, tables and cabinets of rising difficulty (chapter details seen only in search snippets) [uncertain]. AtFAB: 14 current furniture designs plus 4 archived, press-fit and assembled without hardware (Cool Hunting 2012), two of them parametric. Opendesk: about 28 furniture designs; an illustrated joinery post showing about 10 CNC joints (mortise and tenon, slot joint, tooth joint, wedge joint, beam joint, hook joint, a hinge, two Lean Desk joints, a Slim Desk joint, and the 'v-clip locking joint'), a cut-types guide (cut inside/outside/on the line, pocketing, chamfer, fillet, dogbones) and a design-for-CNC guide (sheet size, part spacing, single versus double-sided cutting). Dogbone add-in: three dogbone styles (normal, minimal, mortise) that add round relief cuts to inside corners so square tenons fit
coverage.organisation: Book: project-based, easy to hard, with technique chapters (joinery, toolpaths, parametric design) between projects. AtFAB and Opendesk: product catalogues by furniture type (desks, storage, seating, tables); joint knowledge is in a short three-part Opendesk blog series (cut types, joinery, design for CNC). Dogbone add-in: a single dialog. Beginner-friendly only once you know the furniture you want; no index by joint
coverage.scope_match: medium-low: firmly within the project's woodworking/CNC joinery family (lowest priority), and it includes clever sheet joints (wedged through-tenons, v-clip locking joints, hook joints, press fits without hardware, dogbone relief), but most of the content is whole furniture designs rather than connection types, and the book's joint catalogue sits behind a paywall
coverage.taxonomy_used: Design for CNC: 'joint conditions' by how two sheet parts meet (overlap, edge to edge, end to face, through, three-way, four-way) plus assembly types (S/Z, tab, hanger, corner, foot) [uncertain]. Opendesk: informal list of named joints; cut types classed by tool path (inside, outside, on line, pocket, chamfer, fillet, dogbone). Dogbone add-in: 3 corner-relief styles (normal, minimal, mortise); FabLab RUC adds T-bone as a named variant
coverage.example_types: dogbone corner fillet (router-bit relief, 'dog-bone'); minimal dogbone (tool stops about 0.3 mm short of the corner); T-bone relief (sideways dogbone); mortise-side dogbone (relief hidden along the long side); through mortise and tenon (CNC plywood); wedged through-tenon (tenon locked by a separate wedge through a slot); v-clip locking joint; hook joint (slot-and-hook drop-in joint); tooth joint (interlocking teeth); beam joint; slot joint (cross-halving / egg-crate slot); CNC-cut plywood hinge; S/Z joint (S- or Z-shaped interlocking parts) [uncertain]; tab assembly; hanger assembly; press-fit knock-down joints without hardware (AtFAB); pocket (part-depth recess) joints; snap-finger joints (named in the Maslow forum thread about Opendesk joint files)
coverage.making_methods: CNC routing of sheet material (mainly 18 mm class plywood on 3-axis routers); woodworking assembly; dogbone tools apply to any CNC-milled pocket or slot
coverage.item_count: Design for CNC: 344 pages, 8 basic joint conditions [uncertain]. AtFAB: 14 current plus 4 archived designs. Opendesk: about 28 designs listed; about 10 joints in the joinery post; 3 blog guides. Dogbone: 3 styles
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: Self-locking: yes in a basic way, wedged tenons and the v-clip locking joint hold without glue or screws. Hand-release only / knock-down: AtFAB and Opendesk furniture is meant to assemble (and in some cases disassemble) without hardware [uncertain for disassembly]. Compliant: only a CNC-cut hinge in the Opendesk joinery post (type not verified) [uncertain]. Torque-limiting, one-way/ratchet, indexing/detent, over-centre, print-in-place, gear trains, powered connectors: none. Adhesives: not covered on pages opened (FabLab RUC notes minimal dogbones often give enough friction that glue becomes optional)
coverage.entry_structure: Opendesk joinery post: one exploded and one assembled isometric line drawing per joint with a short caption. Book: step-by-step project chapters with CAD/CAM instructions and technique sidebars [uncertain]. AtFAB/Opendesk products: photo, description, download pack of cut files and assembly guide (Opendesk Studio Desk maker guide PDF exists in the design-playground repo). Dogbone: dialog with tool diameter, radial offset, style and static/parametric mode
coverage.audience_level: hobbyist to professional: makerspace CNC users, design students, and small workshops making furniture commercially

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: medium: Opendesk's illustrated guides and glossary (pocketing, chamfer, fillet) are plain and visual; the book is written as a step-by-step course for makers in schools and makerspaces; dogbone concepts are easy to show but the Fusion add-in assumes CAD skill
usefulness.has_images: yes: Opendesk has clean, consistent isometric line drawings of each joint (exploded and assembled) and of dogbones; the book is illustrated (per publisher description) [uncertain]; AtFAB and Opendesk have product photos; the dogbone README has screenshots of each style
usefulness.has_animations: Opendesk design-playground has browser 3D apps (Three.js) that assemble some Opendesk and AtFAB designs from their DXF files; the Dogbone add-in has a preview mode; no joint animations
usefulness.gaps: No open, browsable catalogue of CNC joint types with names, uses and numbers; the best joint taxonomy (the book's joint conditions) is paywalled; Opendesk's joinery captions are short and give no clearances; few numbers on fit (only FabLab RUC's 0.3 mm minimal dogbone); nothing on metal or plastic sheets, reversible or mechanical behaviours; AtFAB licence terms not clear on the pages opened
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: yes for Opendesk (stable blog URLs such as https://opendesk.cc/blog/digitally-remastered-joinery and product pages such as https://opendesk.cc/designs) and for the Dogbone repo; FabLab RUC dogbone post is a good single link (http://fablab.ruc.dk/more-elegant-cnc-dogbones/). The book can only be cited by chapter
usefulness.reusable_data: Dogbone add-in: MIT-licensed code (reusable). Opendesk cut files: per-design licences, several CC BY or CC0 (Internet Archive 'opendesk' collection, CC BY 4.0 metadata). AtFAB files: open source by the authors' description, licence unverified. Book and blog text/images: not reusable, link or cite only
usefulness.maintained: Opendesk site live (rebuilt 2025; designs and blog online). Filson & Rohrbacher pages live, AtFAB downloads via email sign-up; the older designforcnc.github.io companion site still shows 'Coming Soon'. Dogbone add-in maintained in DVE2000/Dogbone (v2.4; pludikar/dogbone2 closed and moved there). Book in print since 2017, no second edition found
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) Opendesk's paired drawings (exploded view next to assembled view) in one consistent isometric line style, ideal for every connection entry. (2) Design for CNC's 'joint conditions' idea: classify sheet joints by how the parts meet (edge to edge, end to face, through, three-way) as a flow-chart question for the woodwork/CNC family. (3) The dogbone family (normal, minimal, T-bone, mortise-side) as a small 'corner relief' sub-entry that every CNC slot joint links to. (4) Opendesk's clear non-commercial-use definitions as a model for explaining licences of linked files. (5) Project ladders (simple stool to cabinet) as a learning path through joint types
usefulness.design_rules_given: Some. FabLab RUC: with a 3 mm cutter inside corners are left with a 1.5 mm radius; minimal dogbones stop about 0.3 mm short of the corner, nearly invisible, often tight enough to skip glue. Opendesk: leave 20 mm between parts and around the board edge; 1220 x 2440 mm is the common European sheet; prefer single-sided cutting (these numbers are from a search summary of the Opendesk/Medium post, not seen on the opened page) [uncertain]. Dogbone add-in: user sets tool diameter and radial offset. Book: tolerance terms (TMAX, TNOM) and tool-diameter rules are indexed but not verified [uncertain]
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: Yes: the Fusion 360 Dogbone add-in adds static or parametric dogbones (they update when the model changes); AtFAB has two parametric designs (One to Several Table, Open Storage) and the book covers parametric design with Processing; Opendesk design-playground has browser apps with sliders for width, depth, height and material thickness (Slim Chair, Rotational Stools)
usefulness.file_formats: Book: print, ebook. AtFAB: cut files for CNC (book companion lists SketchUp 3D models, DXF/SVG and VCarve CRV 2D files, and Processing apps) [uncertain for current packs]. Opendesk: DXF cut files and PDF maker guides. Dogbone: Fusion 360 Python add-in
usefulness.terminology_value: medium: good for maker/CNC names ('dogbone', 'T-bone', 'minimal dogbone', 'pocketing', 'cut inside/outside the line', 'v-clip locking joint', 'hook joint'); the book's joint-condition vocabulary is distinctive but not widely standard; no translations
usefulness.decision_support: None as such: no selector or comparison table. Opendesk's design-for-CNC post is a checklist of considerations (sheet size, part spacing, single versus double-sided cuts); the dogbone styles are presented with pros and cons (visibility, where the relief hides)
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Opendesk's design-playground and joint repos point to Jochen Gros's '50 Digital Wood Joints' (already researched); the Maslow CNC forum thread and an Internet Archive collection mirror Opendesk files (abetusk). AtFAB designs were also sold through Opendesk (AtFAB range, e.g. Beside Table, One to Several Table, Rotational Stools). Overlaps with WikiHouse (already researched; CNC plywood wedge and peg joints) and with Make:'s 'CNC Panel Joinery Notebook' (Sean Michael Ragan, 2012: edge-lap snap-lock, twist-in, tab-and-slot, captive square nut 'Pettis joint', bulbous finger joints, kanelba hinges, sninges). The Dogbone add-in descends from Casey Rogers' original, modified by Patrick Rainsberry (Autodesk) and David Liu, rewritten by Peter Ludikar and Gary Singer; MakerCase also offers dogbone corner compensation
